dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So many people in Sumeru want to become scholars.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Motivated by this ambition, they all study really hard to try and achieve it...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But Paimon bets that the first ever scholar didn't set out to become a scholar...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... so what do you think the first ever scholar's ambition was?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? But isn't a scholar's ultimate goal supposed to be "pursuing the highest and greatest knowledge" or something?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon's sure that it must have been because of a fervent desire for knowledge that they became Sumeru's first true scholar.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Writing papers is how you pursue knowledge.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But what about when it's the highest and greatest knowledge of all...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Even then, if you wanted to prove it, you'd need a research paper.

choices.text: And after that, you'd need to start working on another paper

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: O—Okay, Paimon's got it! Come on, don't look so sad! It's not like you have to worry about writing papers yourself!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Y—You've never had to write a paper before, right...?

choices.text: To get their research paper written as quickly as possible.
